title: A Performance-testing Platform for a Conduction Micropump with an FR-4 Copper-clad Electrode Plate
protocol: Cut silicone membrane to the same size as the electrode plate.
Use a punching tool to punch chamber holes in the silicone membrane.
Order holder from a factory.
Drill two holes on top of the cover plate for inlet and outlet tubes.
Wash all plates, holder, tubes, and tools with 99.5% acetone using an ultrasonic washer set to 5 minutes.
Insert stainless-steel tubes into the drilled holes in the cover plate.
Place a chamber plate made of silicone membrane on the electrode plate.
Cover the chamber plate with the cover plate.
Stack and align the cover plate, chamber plate, and electrode plate from top to bottom.
Insert the aligned plates into the holder.
Fix the plates inside the holder using an M5 bolt.
Tighten the bolts to press the plates together.
Use a cylinder to inject acetone to fill up the micropump.
Continue injecting 10 mL of acetone inside until all bubbles are pushed away from the chamber.
Pour 20-30 mL of acetone into a beaker.
Submerge the inlet hose in the acetone, ensuring the liquid level is at least 5 mm higher than the hose.
Attach the outlet hose to a small frame to keep it straight and vertical.
Place a ruler alongside the outlet hose for measuring the liquid level.
Connect the micropump to the power source.
Press the switch to start the static pressure test.
Mark down the initial liquid level upon starting the test.
Record the time, final liquid level, and electric current once the liquid level stabilizes.
Continue recording the liquid level and current every 10 seconds until the micropump breaks down.
Use a large measuring cylinder to collect liquid from the outlet hose.
Fix the outlet hose so that its end remains at the same altitude as the liquid level in the beaker.
Connect the micropump to the power source.
Press the switch to start the test and mark down the initial liquid level.
Record the volume of acetone inside the measuring cylinder every 10 seconds.
Add acetone to the beaker to maintain the liquid level throughout the experiment.
